record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is the polynomial-time class P-TIME equal to the nondeterministic polynomial-time class NP-TIME? Equivalently, does every language decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in polynomial time also admit a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P denote the class of languages $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ for which there exists a deterministic Turing machine $M$ and a polynomial $p$ such that $M$ decides $L$ and, on every input $x$, halts within $p(|x|)$ steps. Let NP denote the class of languages $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ for which there exist a deterministic Turing machine $V$ (the verifier) and a polynomial $q$ such that for every $x \in \{0,1\}^*$:
\[ x \in L \iff \exists\, y \in \{0,1\}^{\le q(|x|)} \text{ such that } V(x,y) \text{ accepts within } q(|x|) \text{ steps}. \]
Equivalently, NP is the class of languages decidable by some nondeterministic Turing machine running in time bounded by a polynomial in the input length.

Determine whether $P = NP$. That is, prove or disprove: every language in NP is also in P.
artifact.status_search_result: The P versus NP question is one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems and is universally regarded as a major open problem in mathematics and theoretical computer science. No accepted resolution exists as of 2026.
